$comment: The admitted_launch_envelope.v1 and supervised_run_status.v1 schemas and their conformance vectors are DISTRIBUTED verbatim from the spec repo, where the contract was authored and reviewed; they are frozen, and source sha == shipped sha (normative_source). admitted_launch_envelope.v2 is AUTHORED in this repository, alongside v1, and pinned in authored_here. conformance/SHA256SUMS is the contract's own manifest (paths relative to conformance/): its first five lines are the v1 source manifest byte for byte (distributed.manifest.v1_prefix), followed by one line per v2 file. The contract test suites re-check every digest, so any payload byte change fails them.

authored_here.$comment: Authored and reviewed in this repository; not copied from another source. Harness-neutral and language-neutral, like v1.

consumer_reconciliation.$comment: Attestation recorded at relocation. The contract is provisional: any change needs reconciliation with every consumer before it ships.

v2_consumer_reconciliation.$comment: v2 is additive and every v1 byte is unchanged, so existing v1 pins stay valid. Consumers reconcile v2 when they adopt it, against a published commit and per-file sha256.

verification_scope.$comment: What this package checks without a reader implementation. Full semantic evaluation of every x-semantic-rules diagnostic needs a conforming reader, which consuming harnesses provide.
checked: every shipped byte matches the pinned sha256, and conformance/SHA256SUMS matches the shipped files
schema well-formedness: draft 2020-12, local $refs resolve, known keywords only, closed required sets
every expected diagnostic is defined in the matching schema's x-semantic-rules
every control and every patched negative is schema-valid
envelope_digest self-verifies exactly where envelope_digest_mismatch is not expected
journal segment chains of the controls verify
the v1 payload and the five-line v1 manifest prefix match digests pinned in the test suites independently of this file
v2: every control and semantic negative is schema-valid, and every schema_negative fails with exactly its expected (instance_path, keyword) set

v2: independently written Python and JS readings of x-semantic-rules and x-evaluation-order admit every control and refuse every negative with exactly its expected diagnostics and effect, recomputing every launch digest from the case's captured material

v2: RFC 8785 serialization against pinned serializer primitives (RFC 8785 Appendix B), and the v2 input boundary (safe integers through raw and in-memory paths, duplicate and __proto__ members, lone surrogates) against pinned documents, rejects and wrong preimages, identically in both readings
v2: source-tree capture against pinned manifests, unbindable and ancestor-inconsistent captures, and wrong-walk alternates
v2: the write_scope apply check against pinned outcomes and protected state, and runtime journals against the frozen run-status lifecycle
v2: every new launch field, every semantic rule and every review finding has a positive and a negative vector
not_checked: the remaining semantic diagnostics and expected_effect, which need a conforming reader
v2: a harness's own capture of launch material, its qualification records and evidence, and its apply-time write_scope checker, which need a conforming harness and installed-route qualification
